papers.title: End-to-end Particle Reconstruction with Transformers in High-Granularity Calorimeters
papers.abstract: The High-Luminosity upgrade of the Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC) will drastically increase the number of simultaneously interacting particles, posing a severe challenge to current particle reconstruction methods. While next-generation highly granular calorimeters offer unprecedented 3D measurement capabilities, reconstructing particles from heavily overlapping energy showers remains computationally difficult. This study investigates how raw detector hits can be accurately reconstructed using end-to-end transformer based methods on a simulated calorimeter dataset. We evaluate and compare three distinct machine learning frameworks, focusing on two generative architectures: diffusion and flow matching as well as query-based set prediction. Our results demonstrate that these advanced methods provide highly effective and scalable alternatives for resolving complex overlapping particle showers in conditions encountered in future calorimeters.

papers.title: Position- and Temperature-Dependent Responsivity in a KID-Based Phonon-Mediated Detector
papers.abstract: We report on the position- and temperature-dependent response of a kinetic inductance phonon-mediated (KIPM) detector. To study position-dependence, we used a controllable mirror attached to a micro-electromechanical system (MEMS) to steer optical light with a 100 $\mu$m spot size over the backside of the cryogenic detector. With both pulsed and continuous operation of the LED, we observe features of the detector housing and find that the signal is strongest when the LED is pointed directly at the KID. The "off-KID" response is measured to be 34% of the "on-KID" response and is largely independent of direction. We model phonon propagation and collection in the KIPM detector with G4CMP and assert that the isotropic angular dependence is unlikely to be due to discrete phonon absorption "sinks", such as the microwave feedline or the device mounting points, but can be explained instead by an isotropic energy loss in the crystal. We furthermore utilize the temperature flexibility of the MEMS and KIPM detector system to investigate temperature-dependent responsivity, both at the sensor level (i.e., frequency shifts in the KID) and at the detector level (i.e., position dependence). We fit the KID's response to a two-component heat capacity and present the model as an alternative way to understand the KID's response to absorbed energy. We show on- and off-KID data at a range of temperatures and show that the phonon dynamics are not temperature dependent. We comment on the resulting implication for KID dynamics and design improvements.

papers.title: A flexible electronics and DAQ system for the Timepix4 ASIC
papers.abstract: The INFN Data Acquisition system (IDAQ) is designed for data-driven readout of the Timepix4 ASIC, supporting simultaneous time-of-arrival and time-over-threshold measurements with nanosecond precision. The system architecture combines dedicated hardware for high-speed serial data transmission, FPGA-based data processing, and a Trigger Logic Unit for synchronization and timing distribution. It operates in continuous streaming and triggered modes, ensuring low-latency and high-throughput performance. The system has been deployed in test-beam campaigns within the 4DPHOTON project, demonstrating stable operation, precise timing alignment, and reliable data handling under high-rate conditions.

papers.title: Performance Benchmarks for 2-View and 3-View Fiber-Projection Fine-Grained Particle Detectors
papers.abstract: Fine-grained scintillator detectors are critical for precision measurements in nuclear and particle physics, where accurate reconstruction of interaction vertices and secondary particle directions enables separation of signal from background events. A well-known design choice is the fiber readout geometry: traditional 2-View systems use orthogonal X and Y fibers, while next-generation 3-View designs add a third Z-fiber layer that provides unambiguous 3D voxel identification. The 2-View approach suffers from combinatorial ''ghost hits'', which are false 3D candidates arising from fiber projection ambiguities, that degrade reconstruction performance in high-multiplicity events. This paper presents comprehensive simulation benchmarks quantifying the performance difference between 2-View and 3-View geometries across key metrics. We find that the 3-View geometry reduces ghost hits by 30 to 90% depending on event topology, provides robust vertex resolution across complex topologies, and maintains superior angular resolution for shower direction reconstruction. These benchmarks inform the design optimization of future detectors and provide quantitative guidance for reconstruction algorithm development across a broad range of experiments including neutrino physics, rare kaon/pion decays, and collider calorimetry.

papers.title: Long-term scintillation light performance, calibrations, and triggering efficiency in the MicroBooNE detector
papers.abstract: A detailed understanding of scintillation light in liquid argon time projection chambers (LArTPCs) is essential for the robust extraction of physics measurements from their data. This article presents the long-term performance of scintillation light production and detection using five years of data from the MicroBooNE LArTPC neutrino detector. We describe the MicroBooNE light simulation and light-based triggering schemes, and present the photomultiplier tube gain calibration and stability, light response stability, and light-based systematic uncertainties over the course of five years of data collection. We also make an in-situ measurement of the scintillation light triggering efficiency down to 30 MeV of visible energy. Finally, we discuss two notable observations in MicroBooNE's data, both reported here for the first time: an approximately 50\% decline in MicroBooNE's light yield over time, concentrated in the first two years of running; and a higher than expected O(200 kHz) rate of single photoelectrons (SPE). We present the first measurements of the dependence of the SPE rate on the TPC electric field strength and polarity. Together, the results presented in this article provide an important benchmark for the long-term performance of scintillation light systems in LArTPCs and their use in particle physics measurements.

papers.title: Comprehensive study of timing resolution in plastic scintillator detectors with wavelength-shifting fiber and silicon photomultiplier readout
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive study of the timing resolution achievable in plastic scintillator detectors read out through wavelength-shifting (WLS) fibers coupled to silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs), combining a semi-analytical framework, toy Monte Carlo validation, and full Geant4 optical photon simulation. The analytical model traces the complete photon detection chain: scintillation emission, WLS fiber re-emission, optical transit time dispersion, SiPM single-photon time resolution, and electronics quantization. It expresses the timing resolution $\sigt$ as a function of the detected photoelectron yield $\Npe$, scintillator decay constants ($\taur$, $\taud$), WLS re-emission time ($\tauwls$), fiber numerical aperture, detector geometry, and readout electronics parameters. The analytical predictions are validated at two levels. First, toy Monte Carlo simulations ($2\times 10^5$ events per parameter point across 80 grid points spanning 8 fiber types and $\Npe$ from 5 to 200) achieve analytical-to-MC agreement of \add{$1.0000 \pm 0.0018$}. Second, full Geant4 optical photon simulations track the entire scintillation, wavelength-shifting, and fiber transport chain in realistic detector geometries, confirming the analytical timing predictions\add{ to within 10--20\% for $\Npe \gtrsim 10$} and providing first-principles photoelectron yield calibration. A comprehensive parameter scan covering 7 scintillator materials, 8 WLS fiber types, 5 SiPM models, 5 electronics configurations, 3 readout topologies, and 3 boundary conditions produces quantitative design maps and lookup tables for detector optimization.

papers.title: Transferable Fast Calorimeter Shower Generation via Multi-Geometry Pre-training
papers.abstract: Detailed Geant4 simulation of calorimeter showers dominates the computing budget of high-energy physics experiments. Deep generative surrogates reduce this cost, but they have remained tied to the detector they were trained on, so each new geometry needs a large in-domain dataset. We study whether a single point cloud shower generator can be pre-trained on multiple detectors and transferred to unseen calorimeters. The pre-training geometries come from synthetic geometric variation rather than real-detector data. We introduce SimpleBox, a family of $10^4$ box calorimeters spanning the plane of sampling fraction and longitudinal segmentation, and benchmark it against pre-training on realistic detectors. On a calorimeter unseen in pre-training, with $10^3$ target showers for fine-tuning, the two priors reduce the aggregated sliced Wasserstein distance to Geant4 by factors of 5.2 (synthetic) and 8.0 (realistic) relative to training from scratch. At larger target sizes the synthetic prior performs better than the realistic one. Geometric diversity alone is therefore a practical way to pre-train a transferable shower generator.

papers.title: Converting a superseded Raith electron beam pattern generator into an unattended Critical Dimension SEM
papers.abstract: Design-based metrology of academic electron beam lithography (EBL) is bottlenecked by low-throughput imaging. For integrated photonics, where nanometre-scale structural variation can significantly limit device performance, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is the standard tool for critical dimension (CD) metrology, revealing the structure of devices that is not available from optical measurements. Manual SEM imaging on a wafer-scale is time-intensive, can feature operator-dependent distortions, and yields too few data to reliably close the nanofabrication calibration loop. The following details a methodology that utilises existing hardware in an academic cleanroom: a GDSII-to-SEM software workflow that converts a facility's superseded pattern generator into a CD-SEM for unattended image acquisition and efficient CD and line edge roughness (LER) extraction. This is shown for a Raith eLine Plus, and is expected to be applicable to other pattern generators running Raith's NanoSuite. Presented are results demonstrating its three use cases within a facility: accelerated calibration of two photoresists' process windows; chip-scale metrology of integrated photonic devices to track CD variation; and mass dataset acquisition for convolutional neural network training to predict process distortion. This methodology enables foundry-style, metrology-driven process calibration in academic cleanrooms, generalisable beyond photonics to any EBL nanofabrication that requires nanometre-scale CD control.

papers.title: Neutron spectrometry of (p,n) based neutron fields at the University of Helsinki using the NCT-WES single-moderator directional spectrometer
papers.abstract: A tunable-energy neutron beam produced with up to 1 $\mu$A / 10 MeV proton beam on a solid LiF target is available at the Department of Physics of the University of Helsinki for neutron metrology and research applications. This work presents the experimental characterisation of the neutron beams produced at the Helsinki Accelerator Laboratory, and the validation of the \texttt{MCNP6} and \texttt{GEANT4} radiation transport codes for simulating these neutron beams. The neutron spectra produced in the forward direction from 1960, 2040, and 2310 keV protons were measured using the NCT-WES single-moderator directional spectrometer. NCT-WES (Neutron Capture Therapy Wide Energy Spectrometer) is a recently developed single-moderator neutron spectrometer with a sharply directional response, and it is a very convenient instrument to characterise neutron facilities, as it determines the whole spectrum in a single exposure, and has a low sensitivity to room-scattering. The neutron fluence was also determined with the Berthold LB 6411 neutron monitor. The data acquired with NCT-WES were unfolded using the FRUIT unfolding code, starting from guess spectra obtained from \texttt{GEANT4} or \texttt{MCNP6} simulations. The unfolding analysis showed that both transport codes produced plausible spectra, \texttt{MCNP6} being more accurate for the 1960 and 2040 keV irradiations and \texttt{GEANT4} for 2310 keV. The measured values of energy-integrated neutron fluence agree satisfactorily with simulations as well as preliminary measurements with the LB 6411 neutron monitor.

papers.title: {DEMAND}: {A}n organic glass scintillator array for direct measurements of $(\alpha,n)$ and $(p,n)$ reactions in inverse kinematics
papers.abstract: We have developed an array of up to 20 organic glass scintillator detectors, each consisting of a $3~\mathrm{cm}\times3~\mathrm{cm}\times3~\mathrm{cm}$ scintillator cube coupled to a photomultiplier tube. Sensitive to neutrons from a few hundred keV to several tens of MeV, the array was designed for use with recoil separators in inverse-kinematics measurements of astrophysical $(\alpha,n)$ and $(p,n)$ reactions. It provides a prompt start signal for identifying recoil-neutron coincidences from the recoil time of flight. We characterize eight detectors used in an inverse-kinematics measurement of $^{22}\mathrm{Ne}(\alpha,n)^{25}\mathrm{Mg}$, using source and in-beam data. From the widths of $\gamma$-ray Compton-edge peaks at 311, 341, 477, and 1062 keVee, we find an energy resolution described by $\mathrm{FWHM}(E)/E=\sqrt{A^2/E+B^2/E^2+C^2}$, with $A=0.00(7)$, $B=0.0618(54)$, and $C=0.135(5)$. The time-difference spectrum of nearest-neighbor $\gamma$-$\gamma$ coincidences from a $^{22}\mathrm{Na}$ source (250--600 keVee) gives a FWHM coincidence timing resolution of $910(40)$ ps, corresponding to a single-detector resolution of $640(30)$ ps. Mixed neutron-$\gamma$ fields from the in-beam reaction and a $^{241}\mathrm{AmBe}$ source show pulse-shape discrimination with an $n$-$\gamma$ figure of merit $>1$ down to about 100 keVee. Below 100 keVee, the total neutron yield can still be extracted using two-Gaussian fits to energy-gated pulse-shape discrimination spectra. Monte Carlo simulations of the present $^{22}\mathrm{Ne}(\alpha,n)^{25}\mathrm{Mg}$ measurement give a neutron singles detection efficiency of $1.56(45)%$, with uncertainty dominated by systematic effects in the simulation inputs.

papers.title: Optical Calibration of a Frequency-Domain-Multiplexed X-Ray TES Microcalorimeter Array via Photon-Number-Resolved Statistics
papers.abstract: Transition-edge sensor (TES) microcalorimeters for future X-ray space observatories require accurate low-energy calibration, a regime where conventional X-ray sources are limited by intrinsic linewidth, count rate, or experimental complexity. In this work, we investigate fibercoupled optical photons as a compact calibration tool for an Athena-like TES array. Optical pulses at 405 nm were generated with an acousto-optic modulator and delivered through an optical fiber onto a selected TES pixel inside a dilution refrigerator, via a dedicated cryogenic alignment interface. Externally triggered pulses were processed with an optimal-filter pipeline, including baseline subtraction, drift correction, and multi-Gaussian reconstruction of the pulse-height spectrum. The reconstructed spectra show resolved photon-number peaks consistent with the Poissonian statistics expected from an attenuated coherent source, reaching equivalent energies above 400 eV with a mean photon number exceeding 100 per pulse. The detector response was further tested for linearity by comparing the measured photon-number distributions against those predicted from the independently calibrated number of photons sent to the detector and a single, globally estimated detection efficiency, confirming Poissonian, linear behaviour across nearly two orders of magnitude in photon number. These results demonstrate that fiber-delivered optical photons can probe the few-eV to sub-keV response of Athena-like TES microcalorimeters, offering a practical and extensible framework for future low-energy calibration studies.

papers.title: Extending the limits of rotationally resolved mid-IR spectroscopy: an accurate model of trioxane derived from combining Fourier transform and sub-Doppler measurements
papers.abstract: 1,3,5-Trioxane, a polyoxymethylene (POM) molecule relevant to prebiotic chemistry and astrophysics, exhibits a dense rovibrational spectrum that challenges high-resolution spectroscopic characterization. Here, we report an extensive study of its $\nu$ 5 CO symmetric stretching mode (960-1000 cm -1 ) by combining broadband high-resolution FTIR spectroscopy (0.001 cm -1 resolution, >2000 transitions) with SI-traceable sub-Doppler saturated absorption measurements using frequency-stabilized CO 2 lasers and a frequency-comb-referenced quantum cascade laser. The latter achieve lineposition uncertainties as low as 40 kHz, revealing inaccuracies in the FTIR frequency scale. A frequency-scale correction is determined by maximizing the global consistency of the complete spectroscopic data set. A global least-squares Hamiltonian fit combining the calibrated FTIR data, the SI-traceable sub-Doppler measurements and previously reported millimeter-wave rotational transitions yields a refined spectroscopic model. The resulting analysis significantly improves the precision of the rotational, quartic, and sextic constants for both the ground and $\nu$ 5 excited vibrational states. This work extends mid-infrared frequency metrology to the largest molecule studied to date (12 atoms), providing a dense set of reference transitions for frequency calibration around 970 cm -1 . The resulting spectroscopic parameters reach relative uncertainties as low as 3.7 x 10 -10 for the band origin, making them valuable for molecular databases used in astrophysics and atmospheric physics, as well as for precision measurements in fundamental physics. Additionally, the observed line shapes indicate the absence of significant intramolecular vibrational energy redistribution (IVR) within the investigated energy range, while a few discrepancies in the Hamiltonian fit suggest the onset of weak perturbations, demonstrating the sensitivity of the present approach to probe subtle intramolecular couplings in complex polyatomic spectra. papers.title: Absolute calibration of scintillators for laser-driven ion spectroscopy using in situ CR-39 sampling detectors
papers.abstract: Quantitative studies of laser-driven ion acceleration and laser-induced nuclear fusion require accurate measurements of ion yields and energy spectra. Although scintillator screens integrated with Thomson parabola spectrometers provide real-time diagnostics, their nonlinear scintillation response requires absolute calibration. We present an in situ, single-shot cross-calibration method using a 2-mm-period CR-39 sampling mask to simultaneously record particle counts and scintillation signals from laser-accelerated proton beams. The method is applied to calibrate a 400-$\mu$m-thick CsI:Tl crystal and a 6-$\mu$m-thick P43 phosphor screen over a broad proton energy range. The measured scintillation responses are compared with a theoretical model combining Birks' law and simulated proton stopping powers. The calibration quantitatively reveals the distinct response characteristics of the two scintillators, including thickness-dependent punch-through effects and constraints on ionization quenching, and demonstrates a practical approach for the absolute calibration of scintillator screens used in laser-driven ion spectroscopy.

papers.title: Automated CR-39 pit detection for energy and angular characterization of laser-driven ion beams
papers.abstract: Accurate characterization of ion beams from sub-MeV to multi-MeV energies is essential for diagnostics in laser-driven ion acceleration and fusion research. CR-39 detectors are widely used to measure absolute ion yields, while ion energy and incidence angle can be inferred from etched-pit geometries. In this study, we present an automated CR-39 pit detection method that enables reliable extraction of pit geometries from two-dimensional optical micrographs, with improved discrimination of overlapping pits under high-flux conditions. This capability enables reliable analysis in high-density regimes where conventional methods are limited by significant track overlap. By integrating the detected pit shapes with a pit-formation model based on Monte Carlo simulations of restricted energy loss, energy and angular characterization of laser-driven proton beams is achieved with enhanced precision and computational efficiency. The proposed framework provides a robust and scalable approach for automated CR-39 analysis and is applicable to a broad range of ion-beam diagnostics and spectroscopy.

papers.title: Stability Study of Photo-inscribed Bragg Gratings in Sapphire Fibers at Very High Temperature
papers.abstract: Fiber Bragg gratings inscribed by femtosecond laser in sapphire fibers were subjected to thermal cycling up to 1500$\degree$C. Adding a multimode silica fiber reduces modal interference, improves the quality of the Bragg spectrum and the measurement accuracy. The measurement uncertainty is about 1.9$\degree$C at 1500$\degree$C.

papers.title: New muon transfer cell for muonic x-ray spectroscopy on microgram-quantity targets based on liquid hydrogen
papers.abstract: The muon transfer method allows access to radioactive/rare atomic nuclei for determining their charge radii via muonic x-ray spectroscopy. In this study we present a new muon transfer cell based on liquid hydrogen optimized for low-energy x-ray spectroscopy by employing a thin-walled Mylar cell for the container of the liquid hydrogen. Based on simulations, the present liquid hydrogen cell achieves competitive efficiencies compared to existing devices using the muon transfer method. Additionally, the liquid-hydrogen-based muon transfer setup provides a short timescale for the diffusion process of the muonic hydrogen atoms in the cell, well below 200~ns.

papers.title: Simulation-Derived Angular Migration in Volcanic Muography
papers.abstract: Transmission muography usually treats each angular bin as a straight line of sight through the target. Multiple Coulomb scattering can break this mapping by changing the muon direction in rock. We introduce CABRIALES, a reduced model that represents this effect as migration between source and destination angular bins. The input muons are generated with a conditional normalizing flow trained on ARTI simulations, selected with a continuous-slowing-down range threshold, and deflected using angular distributions derived from Geant4. We apply the model to four observation points at Cerro Machin volcano in Colombia. Among the muons selected by the transmission threshold, 41.4-45.1% move to a different 2.5-degree bin within the field of view, while 20.7-24.3% reach a different rock-intersecting angular bin associated with a longer rock path in the terrain model. For muons with energies within 5% above the transmission threshold, the changed-bin fraction increases to 67.4-81.3%. Destination maps further show that events arriving from shorter assigned paths can form a large share of the modeled population in some rock-intersecting bins. These results quantify angular redistribution before detector response; they do not represent net count changes or density bias.

papers.title: Simulating scintillation detector responses with OpenMC and pyMPPost: a track-based coupling verified against MCNPX-PoliMi
papers.abstract: Simulations of the detector response are essential for the design and analysis of neutron and photon measurements in nuclear nonproliferation, safeguards, and active interrogation studies. MCNPX-PoliMi, combined with the post-processor MPPost and its Python implementation pyMPPost, is a well-established and validated framework for this purpose. Its detector models, however, are not available to users of the open-source Monte Carlo code OpenMC, which does not write an equivalent collision-level output. This work couples OpenMC to pyMPPost, allowing the open-source community to use the detector models already implemented and validated in pyMPPost without modifying either code. A Python class, $\texttt{TrackAnalyzer}$, reads the particle tracks written by OpenMC, reconstructs the interactions in the detector material along with the target nuclide and writes them in the MCNPX-PoliMi collision file format. The method relies only on the track output and is therefore applicable to any OpenMC version that writes particle tracks, including the development branch with photonuclear physics used in this work. The coupling was verified code to code against MCNPX-PoliMi for a trans-stilbene and a $^{4}$He scintillator exposed to $^{252}$Cf and deuterium-deuterium fusion neutron sources, and for a NaI(Tl) scintillator exposed to $^{137}$Cs and $^{152}$Eu photon sources. The total number of pulses agrees within $\pm$1\% in all cases, and the light-output spectra agree within a few percent in the covered spectral domain. By making the detector response models of pyMPPost available within a fully open-source simulation chain, this work extends detector response studies with OpenMC to nuclear nonproliferation and active interrogation applications, including those involving photonuclear reactions, and provides an accessible tool for education and training in radiation detection.

papers.title: Unlimited-Range Absolute Distance Interferometry Outdoors via Tunable Synthetic and Pseudo-Supersynthetic Wavelengths: The TeleYAG-II Interferometer
papers.abstract: Absolute distance interferometry requires an unlimited non-ambiguity range to be truly absolute. Tunable synthetic wavelength interferometry allows for the construction of pseudo-supersynthetic wavelengths using a limited number of optical sources and a standard interferometer setup. This approach facilitates the creation of a series of consecutively deployable synthetic wavelengths, ultimately combining macroscopic unambiguity with microscopic interferometric accuracy. We have implemented and demonstrated this concept in the TeleYAG-II interferometer, designed as an SI-traceable standard for the calibration of geodetic baselines. The system employs two Nd:YAG lasers as optical sources, with their frequency difference controlled by a versatile optical phase-locked loop. Specifically engineered for robustness in field conditions, the heterodyne interferometer was validated through an outdoor measurement campaign. The results demonstrate the efficacy of the method, achieving an expanded measurement uncertainty of 0.13 mm over a distance of 224 m without the need for auxiliary length measurements.

papers.title: Photon-starved imaging through turbulence at the diffraction limit
papers.abstract: Atmospheric turbulence limits the resolution of ground-based imaging through rapidly evolving wavefront distortions. Fast acquisition can effectively freeze turbulence, but the restricted photon budget makes joint scene and wavefront recovery challenging. Here, we introduce Turbulence-Aware Poisson Blind Deconvolution (TAP-BD), which uses optical phase diversity to provide complementary measurements within a short acquisition window and increase wavefront information per detected photon. Poisson denoising and physics-informed optimization translate this information gain into joint recovery of the scene and a shared turbulence wavefront, with phase estimation errors approaching the Cramer--Rao lower bound in simulations. Experiments demonstrate reliable recovery from only a few tens of measurements under strong turbulence, with additional validation under severe photon scarcity. Simulations further show robustness to scintillation and temporal evolution over short acquisition windows. These results support photon-efficient imaging through turbulence, with potential applications in astronomy, remote sensing, and space situational awareness, particularly for time-sensitive observations.

papers.title: Charge-Carrier transport simulations in diamond detectors with electric-field-dependent mobility and charge-collection-distance-based trapping
papers.abstract: Diamond detectors are attractive for operation in harsh radiation environments because they combine radiation tolerance, fast signal formation, and low leakage current. Realistic detector-response simulations require an accurate description of charge-carrier mobility and trapping, which determine both signal amplitude and timing. In this work, we extend \allpix{}, a modular end-to-end detector simulation framework, with diamond-specific transport models. The implementation includes field-dependent mobility parameterizations for electrons and holes and an effective trapping model based on the charge collection distance (CCD), providing a detector-level interface to material quality and radiation-damage measurements. The mobility description is validated in the negligible-trapping limit using single-crystalline CVD diamond by comparing simulated drift velocities and transient-current signals with published reference data. For polycrystalline CVD diamond, the CCD-based trapping model is evaluated using experimentally measured CCD values and compared with laboratory transient-current-technique waveforms. The simulations reproduce the measured drift-velocity behavior in scCVD and the reduced charge collection and degraded transient response observed in pcCVD. The presented implementation enables detector-level studies of charge collection, pulse formation, and timing performance in diamond sensors using experimentally accessible transport and trapping parameters, and provides a practical framework for simulation-driven detector development and radiation-damage studies.

papers.title: A new diffuse reflector filament for additive manufacturing of 3D printing finely-segmented plastic scintillator
papers.abstract: This study presents the development and the characterisation of a novel white, reflective filament suitable for additive manufacturing of finelysegmented plastic scintillators. The filament is based on polycarbonate (PC) and polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) polymers loaded with titanium dioxide (TiO$_2$) and polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) to enhance reflectivity. A range of filament compositions and thicknesses was evaluated through optical reflection and transmittance measurements of reflective layers made with the Fused Deposition Modelling (FDM) technique. A 3D-segmented plastic scintillator prototype was made with fused injection modelling (FIM) and tested with cosmic-ray muons to assess the light yield and the optical crosstalk. The results of this study demonstrate the feasibility of producing compact, modular 3D-printed scintillator detectors with a performance comparable to that of standard plastic scintillator detectors whilst exhibiting lower light crosstalk and higher light yield, owing to the improved optical properties of the reflector material.

papers.title: RPC Telescope Tests for Muon Detection at Laser-Plasma Accelerators
papers.abstract: We report on a feasibility study conducted at the ELBA facility at ELI Beamlines in 2025 to investigate the possible production of muons from high-energy electron beams generated by extended laser-plasma interactions in optically generated plasma waveguides. Our team operated a portable, autonomous, and compact telescope based on Resistive Plate Chamber (RPC) detectors, positioned to detect high-penetration charged particles originating from the beam dump. The campaign demonstrated that RPC detectors can operate reliably and safely in the ELBA environment, even under intense radiation and electromagnetic conditions. The collected datasets, though statistically limited and affected by lack of beam control, allow detailed characterization of the background and validated the detectors' stability and tracking performance. These results confirm the feasibility of the approach and provide the foundation for a dedicated future run under optimized beam conditions, where muon detection sensitivity will be substantially improved.

papers.title: Readout chain of SPD DAQ system
papers.abstract: The Spin Physics Detector (SPD) experiment at the NICA collider of the Joint Institute for Nuclear Research (JINR) aims to study the spin structure of the nucleon and spin-related phenomena. The experimental conditions, including the high interaction rate and the large number of readout channels, require a triggerless data acquisition system with high throughput and a scalable architecture. This work presents a hardware implementation of the readout chain that extends the previously proposed SPD DAQ architecture. The chain is based on two levels of concentrators. The L1 concentrator provides the interface between the front-end electronics and the next system level and distributes synchronous signals. The L2 concentrator aggregates data streams from several L1 concentrators before transmitting them to the computing system. A key feature of the L2 implementation is the offloading of data reception, buffering, and aggregation from the host CPU to the FPGA, motivated by the large number of small packets generated by the readout electronics. The developed hardware platforms and their operating logic are presented, together with experimental results for the main interfaces and data-path components. The obtained results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed hardware architecture and its application in a scalable SPD data acquisition system.
